finding_that_reverses_two_prior_records.what: The producer reports, and the Coordinator independently confirmed, that the value 49 IS PRINTED IN THE PUBLISHED SPECIFICATION. Page 18 of the PDF text layer reads verbatim: 'RS-S3[90 = 255 -165, 32 = 197 -165, 49].'
finding_that_reverses_two_prior_records.coordinator_verification: The Coordinator re-acquired hqc_specifications_2025_08_22.pdf independently (sha256 174186cb...5406d, byte-identical to BATCH-001's record and a fourth independent fetch) and extracted the line from the text layer directly.
finding_that_reverses_two_prior_records.what_this_falsifies: BATCH-002-OPENING.md section 3, the BATCH-002 opening commit message, and BATCH-001 red-team objection O1 all attribute the 49 to the TRANSCRIPTION. That attribution is FALSE. TASK-20260802-6344ed transcribed faithfully and its classification of X6 as a SOURCE anomaly was correct.
finding_that_reverses_two_prior_records.what_survives_and_is_stronger: The numeric correction to 59 stands on three routes internal to the specification, needing no external MDS theory: the spec's own shortening arithmetic (255-165 and 197-165 subtract 165 from both n and k, so n-k=58 is invariant and d=n-k+1=59); Table 3's delta=29 giving 2*29+1=59; and the printed generator polynomial g3 having degree 58=2*delta, a route named by neither the handoff nor either BATCH-001 review.
finding_that_reverses_two_prior_records.why_the_source_says_49: 49 = 80-32+1 is CORRECT for the n=80 external code in RMRS Figure 6. The specification moved n from 80 to 90 and did not update d. A stale published parameter, not a random typo.
finding_that_reverses_two_prior_records.consequence: CORR-20260802-3ae664 must correct the SPECIFICATION's value and must NOT assert the transcription erred. Recorded here so the reviewers see the reversal before the ledger archive fixes it.
